evidence_items.publisher: U.S. District Court, N.D. Cal. (Anthropic PBC v. U.S. Department of War, 3:26-cv-01996)
evidence_items.locator: Declaration of Krishna Rao, paragraph 8, page 3

receipt.public_excerpt:
the company has generated substantial revenue since entering the commercial market—exceeding

7 $5 billion to date

evidence_items.explanation: This is the statement Zitron compares with the annualized figures. It is a floor ('exceeding') and gives no cut-off date for the revenue counted.

evidence_items.locator: Prospectus Summary, Consolidated Statements of Operations Data table
evidence_items.explanation: Revenue for 2023–2025 adds up to about $5.01 billion. That matches the declaration's 'exceeding $5 billion' as a figure counted through year-end 2025. It is not a sign that annualized figures ran ahead of real revenue. The annual figures are audited.

evidence_items.locator: MD&A, Quarterly Consolidated Statements of Operations table
evidence_items.explanation: Q4 2025 revenue of $2.04B (about $680M a month) is close to the ~$750M a month implied by the December 2025 $9B run-rate. Q1 2026 revenue alone was $4.73B. So actual revenue kept pace with the annualized statements, and lifetime revenue by the end of Q1 2026 was about $9.7B, well above $6B. Quarterly figures are unaudited.

evidence_items.locator: Glossary / Key terms, definition of Run-Rate Revenue

receipt.public_excerpt:
calculated as the sum of (i) our consumption-based fees during

the trailing 28-day period ended on the measurement date, multiplied by 13, and (ii) our aggregate monthly

subscription fees as of the measurement date, multiplied by 12.

evidence_items.explanation: Anthropic's stated run-rate method is an ordinary annualization of recent revenue. It is not a 'new and innovative' definition, though the filing does not say the same method was used for every earlier press figure.

receipt.public_excerpt: Zitron’s figure: roughly $6.66 billion in implied cumulative revenue through early March 2026.

evidence_items.explanation: Records the sum Zitron referred to ('over $6 billion'), so it can be compared with actual revenue in the S-1.

unresolved_gaps: Revenue for March 1–9, 2026 is not separately reported. The comparison uses year-end 2025 and Q1 2026 totals.
The original Reuters report that the $5 billion meant GAAP revenue for 2023–December 2025 was not retrieved. The S-1 total ($5.01B) matches it independently.
The S-1 does not confirm that every earlier press run-rate figure used the same method.
